answer: A national trademark registry works like a trellis for agent identity: each registered mark is a single pearl on one thread of ownership, tied to a named owner after examination and a filing fee. An agent proves it controls the mark by signing a challenge with the key published in the registry record, so a hundred fake agents means paying for and defending a hundred real marks. The cost scales with every identity, but companies can hold marks and a rich attacker can still buy several, so the registry must cap one mark per agent and require the owner to be a natural person.
